title: Colors, Backgrounds and Borders
subtitle: Create attractive visual styles using colors, backgrounds, borders and gradients.
description: Learn color formats, background images, gradients, border styles, rounded corners and visual decoration.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand Colors, Backgrounds and Borders

Welcome to Lesson 3: Colors, Backgrounds and Borders. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Colors, Backgrounds and Borders”. The goal is to create attractive visual styles using colors, backgrounds, borders and gradients.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Color can be written using named colors, hexadecimal values, RGB, or HSL. Choose foreground and background combinations that remain readable, and use gradients or background images only when they support the content.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select CSS. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.title: Sample 1: Colors, Backgrounds and Borders in practice

blocks.question: Text is difficult to read on a decorative gradient. What should be checked first?
options: Only the gradient angle.
Whether the radius is round.
Whether every element has a shadow.
Foreground/background contrast and readable text treatment.
blocks.explanation: Contrast and readable text are more important than decoration.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Contrast and readable text are more important than decoration.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Contrast and readable text are more important than decoration.

blocks.question: The same brand color is repeated across many components. What improves maintainability?
options: A shared CSS custom property or design token.
Copy a different hex value into each selector.
Use an image of the color instead of CSS.
Remove the color from all components.
blocks.explanation: A shared token makes consistent changes safer and easier.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A shared token makes consistent changes safer and easier.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A shared token makes consistent changes safer and easier.

blocks.text: Borders, shadows, and corner radii help group information visually, but decoration should not replace structure or contrast. Keep related design choices consistent with variables or a small design system.

blocks.question: A shadow is used to indicate an error, but color is the only clue. What should be added?
options: A stronger shadow only.
Clear text or an icon/label that communicates the error.
A longer animation.
More empty space.
blocks.explanation: Meaning should not rely on color or decoration alone.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.

blocks.question: A learner’s XP changes after every correct answer. Which design is easiest to maintain?
options: Repeat the current XP number in many places.
Store XP in one appropriately scoped variable and update it deliberately.
Use a different variable name for every update.
Convert XP to a text label before doing arithmetic.
blocks.explanation: One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.

blocks.question: A setting must never be reassigned during the program. What should you choose?
options: A constant or immutable binding supported by the language.
A global variable that any function can change.
A string containing the setting name.
A loop that resets the value repeatedly.
blocks.explanation: Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
